runAssessment.summary: The run was cancelled by user signal after 795 seconds and $0.23582544, before any deliverable or final acceptance was recorded. It made useful progress on the first of three sequential branches, producing and repeatedly testing the service, while validators correctly continued to reject incomplete proof coverage. The retries added tests and evidence rather than merely repeating work, so the cancellation policy behaved as intended and the observed spend does not establish avoidable waste.

findings.title: Cancellation interrupted an improving but still unaccepted first branch
findings.detail: All three Methane executions were uncredited, but they were not identical retries: the final execution expanded the subprocess test from 2,243 to 4,465 bytes, exposed and corrected an assertion mismatch, and obtained passing executions. Independent validation still showed weak requirement confidence and recorded failure before cancellation interrupted skill processing. Because no final result was delivered, these passing checks prove only their visible narrow assertions, not satisfaction of the full stock-reservation contract.

planning.summary: Meristem selected a Node HTTP-oriented decomposition with three sequential branches, and Methane produced plans that underwent explicit plan validation before execution. Later plans incorporated validator coaching about concurrency, expiration ordering, restart persistence, seed validation, and exact responses.

delegation.summary: Routing selected Meristem, then the specialized Sclereid cell, which delegated the first branch to Methane. The branch hierarchy and single-child concat handoff were coherent for a Node HTTP service; cancellation occurred before the remaining sequential branches began.

execution.summary: Methane created server.js, package.json, README.md, and real subprocess tests, recovered from initial implementation and harness failures, and exercised live HTTP endpoints. Three executions consumed 27, 14, and 19 tool calls; all were completed but uncredited because result validation never accepted the branch. The later executions added coverage and corrected discovered assertions, so they were progressive rather than identical repetition.

validation.summary: Validation included plan gates, three result-review rounds, subprocess executions, and recorded live HTTP probes. Narrow observations established initial state, literal __proto__ handling, invalid-command refusal, confirmation, and deterministic state reads. The test bodies are truncated in the digest, so the passing suite cannot establish every compound requirement; appropriately, the final validator remained unconvinced and no acceptance or delivery followed.

recovery.summary: Recovery was adaptive: an idempotency test failure led to canonicalization and fixture corrections; server-tool incompatibilities led to startup adjustments; validator rejections led to expanded tests. A prohibited manual probe-manifest edit was refused by the tool. The run then ended by user cancellation rather than an internal failure.
